name: rightsize
description: Stop paying Opus prices for Haiku work. rightsize matches each Claude Code prompt to the right model and effort, so your budget and usage limits go further. It learns from how you work, and you can configure every part of it. You stay in charge: it asks before it acts, shows each change it makes, and /rightsize report shows whether it's paying off.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: How much evidence rightsize needs before it picks a cheaper route. Quality: cheaper routes only with strong evidence (at least 10 logged tasks of that kind on that route, under 10% misses, and the route under 50% of staying), raises readily, gives a struggling helper 1 retry. Balanced (default): a cheaper route when the rating says it fits and it is under 70% of staying; pauses a kind of work at 20% misses; 2 retries. Economy: cheaper routes on fit alone, under 85% of staying, paused only at 30% misses; 3 retries. A profile also sets how often Sonnet checks Haiku's ratings (every 10, 20 or 30), which answer each of the four questions lists first, marked (Recommended), and what happens before a big session's cache goes cold (Quality keeps it warm for 8 hours; Balanced and Economy ask). Every row below is Advanced: a row you set always wins over the profile.

floor.title: Advanced · Lowest effort
floor.description: The lowest effort level rightsize will lower to.

ceiling.title: Advanced · Highest effort
ceiling.description: The highest effort level rightsize will raise to. It never goes above this: not when a prompt needs more, not mid-turn when Claude looks stuck (those also never reach max), and not for the subagent it hands work to, which runs at most at this level. A level you are already on above it is left alone: this stops raises, it never lowers.

lowerRule.title: Advanced · Lowering
lowerRule.description: What to do when a prompt needs less effort. ask me: ask each time. lower automatically: lower without asking. never lower: never. not set: ask the first time it comes up (the default). A rule set here is used as it is and its question is never asked. The band's buttons and /rightsize settings set it too; set it back to not set to be asked again. Which answer the question lists first, marked (Recommended), depends on your Profile.

raiseRule.title: Advanced · Raising
raiseRule.description: What to do when a prompt needs more effort on the same model. ask me: ask each time. raise automatically: raise without asking. never raise: never. not set: ask the first time it comes up (the default). This rule also decides raises mid-turn when Claude looks stuck. A rule set here is used as it is and its question is never asked, even when a usage window is nearly used up. Which answer the question lists first, marked (Recommended), depends on your Profile.

upRule.title: Advanced · Stronger model
upRule.description: What to do when a stronger model than yours would do better. ask first: ask before sending the work to a subagent on it. always send: send it without asking. stay, raise effort only: stay on your model and raise effort. ask each time: ask what to do each time. not set: ask the first time it comes up (the default). A rule set here is used as it is and its question is never asked, even when a usage window is nearly used up. Which answer the question lists first, marked (Recommended), depends on your Profile.

downRule.title: Advanced · Cheaper model
downRule.description: What to do when a task could run on a cheaper model than yours. ask first: ask before sending it to a subagent on that model. always send: send it without asking. stay, lower effort only: stay on your model and lower effort. ask each time: ask what to do each time. not set: ask the first time it comes up (the default). A rule set here is used as it is and its question is never asked. Which answer the question lists first, marked (Recommended), depends on your Profile.

remember.title: Advanced · Remember choices
remember.description: What happens to your answers to the four questions above. ask: after your first answer, ask whether to use your choices in every session (the default). every session: keep every answer for later sessions, without asking. this session: never keep an answer and never ask; answers last until the session ends. A rule set in its row above is always kept.

handOff.title: Advanced · Hand-off threshold
handOff.description: Send a big task to a cheaper subagent only when it is estimated to cost under this share of staying on your model, counting the brief, check and likely rework. Lower is stricter. Left alone, your Profile sets it: Quality 50%, Balanced 70%, Economy 85%.

lowering.title: Advanced · Lowering threshold
lowering.description: Lower effort only when the lower level is estimated to cost under this share of staying, counting the cache it may rewrite. Lower is stricter.

useHaiku.title: Advanced · Use Haiku
useHaiku.description: on: rightsize may hand work to Haiku, and move Claude's own subagents to it. off: it never does, and the starting-point comparison leaves Haiku out. Haiku still rates your prompts (it is the rater, not a worker), so this does not stop the rating calls.

useFable.title: Advanced · Use Fable
useFable.description: on: rightsize may hand work to Fable when the work needs a stronger model. off: it never does, and the starting-point comparison leaves Fable out. If you work on Fable yourself, nothing changes.

subagents.title: Advanced · Claude's subagents
subagents.description: cheaper when it fits: when Claude starts a general-purpose subagent without naming a model, rate its brief and run it on the cheapest weaker model that fits, at that model's level, under the hand-off threshold. off: leave Claude's own subagents on its model.

workflows.title: Advanced · Workflows
workflows.description: What rightsize does once Claude starts a workflow (ultracode, or asked for): many helper agents at once, often 10 or more, each picking its own model. ask: ask before the first workflow starts (the default); until you answer, rightsize pauses for it. pause rightsize: hand nothing off for the rest of the session, and leave the workflow's agents alone. follow my rules: hand-offs follow your Stronger model and Cheaper model rules as usual; the workflow's agents are left alone. right-size every agent: as follow my rules, and each workflow agent that names no model is rated by Haiku (one rating call each) and runs on the cheapest model that fits, under Claude's subagents, Use Haiku, Use Fable and Pause after misses. Claude's subagents set to off keeps the agents alone in every case. Whichever you pick, measurement stays paused after a workflow: calibration learns nothing and no saving is claimed.

explore.title: Advanced · Explore close calls
explore.description: on: when two models that fit cost about the same, rightsize picks by task type, and one close call in five takes the other model so both get measured. off (default): a close call always takes the task-type pick, so the other model may never be measured.

missPause.title: Advanced · Pause after misses
missPause.description: Haiku's rating is scored against what happens: rework on hand-offs, lowered turns that stepped back up, mid-turn raises, your 👍 and 👎, and Sonnet's checks. When its miss rate for a kind of work on a model reaches this share, rightsize stops handing that work down to that model and stops lowering effort on it, until the rate falls back under it. off: never pause. Left alone, your Profile sets it: Quality pauses at 10% misses and also needs at least 10 logged tasks of that kind on that model before it uses a cheaper route, Balanced pauses at 20%, Economy at 30%. A value you set here replaces the whole rule.

pacing.title: Advanced · Budget pacing
pacing.description: on: on a subscription, move the thresholds by how fast the 5-hour and 7-day windows are being used. Running out early: hand off and lower more readily. Much left near a reset: hand off only for big savings. Over 90% used: save all it can, which skips raises and stronger models while Raising and Stronger model are not set. A threshold or rule you set stays as you set it: pacing moves only what is left at its default. off: always use the thresholds above.

escalation.title: Advanced · Raise when stuck
escalation.description: on: when a turn shows Claude is stuck (see Stuck sensitivity), raise effort one level for the rest of the turn, at most twice, never above Highest effort and never to max. It follows your Raising rule: automatic raises without asking, otherwise it asks. off: never raise mid-turn.

stuck.title: Advanced · Stuck sensitivity
stuck.description: How soon Claude counts as stuck. normal: the same tool call failing twice, 3 tool calls failing, the same call running 3 times, or a turn passing 3x the rated steps (at least 15). relaxed: the same call failing 3 times, 4 calls failing, a call running 4 times, or 4x the steps (at least 20). sensitive: the same call failing twice, 2 calls failing, a call running twice, or 2x the steps (at least 10).

rater.title: Advanced · Rater
rater.description: sonnet or haiku: the model that rates each prompt (and each subagent brief), at low effort. sonnet (default) reads prompts more reliably; haiku costs less per rating. With sonnet, a rating that times out, is refused or comes back unreadable is tried once more on Haiku; with haiku, a timeout or an unreadable answer is tried once more on Haiku.

raterCheck.title: Advanced · Rater check
raterCheck.description: every 25, every 50 or every 100: on every that many prompts rated by Haiku (Rater set to haiku, or Sonnet failed), ask Sonnet in the background to rate the same prompt, and log where it says a model would struggle that Haiku said does the work. These checks and the other outcomes give a miss rate per task type and model (see Pause after misses). Each check costs one Sonnet call and never delays the prompt. off: no checks (the other outcomes still count). Left alone, your Profile sets it: every 10 (Quality), every 20 (Balanced) or every 30 (Economy).

startTips.title: Advanced · Start suggestions
startTips.description: weekly or monthly: every 7 or 30 days, estimate what the last 30 days of rated prompts would have cost from Sonnet and Opus at medium and high, rightsize's changes counted. Prompts Haiku's rating has often got wrong for a model count against that model's start. When another start is at least 15% cheaper (25% while it has few measured runs) without sending over 1 prompt in 10 to a stronger model, or when over 15% of prompts needed a stronger model or more effort, the band suggests switching with /model. rightsize never changes your model itself. off: no suggestions; /rightsize report still shows the comparison.

idleWarning.title: Advanced · Idle warning
idleWarning.description: When a session under 200K tokens sat idle past the cache's life (1 hour, or 5 minutes when prices.json says 5m), ask before the next prompt writes the whole conversation to the cache again, when that costs over this much more than a warm cache. You can send it or hold it to /clear or /compact first. On a subscription the bar is in API-equivalent dollars, and the question gives the cost as a share of the 5-hour window once runs show the rate.

beforeCold.title: Advanced · Before the cache goes cold
beforeCold.description: What rightsize does when a session that ends a turn with a big conversation (a cold return would cost $0.50 or more, API-equivalent on a subscription; under 200K tokens) is about to lose its prompt cache. ask: offer the choices in the band, each with its cost, and do nothing if you do not pick. keep warm 2 h, keep warm 8 h: send one tiny request just before each expiry to keep the cache warm until then, and stop when you type, press Stop, a request fails, or keeping warm would cost more than coming back cold. save a handoff: run Groundwork's wrap-up once before expiry (compact when Groundwork is not installed). compact: compact once before expiry. off: nothing. Nothing runs during a turn. Not set here, Profile decides: Quality keeps warm for 8 hours; Balanced and Economy ask.

billing.title: Advanced · Reports
billing.description: api: subagent reports show dollars. subscription: they show the share of usage and of the 5-hour window, with API-equivalent dollars beside it. rightsize reads this off each response's rate limits when they show it. A value set here is your answer: the rate limits never change it, and /rightsize says when they disagree.

band.title: Advanced · Band
band.description: The row above the prompt that shows what rightsize did, with buttons to retry it at the original effort, mark a hand-off or lowering 👍 or 👎 (kept on this machine) or change the rule. when it acts: only when it changes something. always: on every rated prompt, no change included. off: status line only.

share.title: Advanced · Share anonymous feedback
share.description: on: send anonymous numbers to the rightsize author, at most once an hour, to tune its defaults: task types, models, effort levels, rated levels, token guesses, estimated and real costs, what went wrong, Sonnet checks, and your 👍 and 👎, with a random install id. Never prompts, code, file names, paths, tool or server names, or session ids. Only what is logged after you turn it on is sent. off (default): nothing is sent; turning it off and on again starts a new install id.

priceCheck.title: Advanced · Price check
priceCheck.description: monthly: compare prices.json with Anthropic's pricing page every 30 days and update it. off: never check. /rightsize prices checks right away, whatever this says.
